H1: ARTICLE VI — INSOLVENCY PROCEEDINGS
S: 6.1|DIP Financing; Use of Cash Collateral|(a) Until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations has occurred, if any Grantor shall be subject to any Insolvency Proceeding and the First Lien Agent shall desire to permit the use of cash collateral (as such term is defined in Section 363(a) of the Bankruptcy Code) on which the First Lien Agent or any other creditor has a Lien, or to permit any Grantor to obtain financing, whether from the First Lien Secured Parties or any other Person, under Section 364 of the Bankruptcy Code or any similar provision of any other Bankruptcy Law (each, a “**DIP Financing**”), then the Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that it (i) consents to, and shall not object to, contest or otherwise oppose (or support any other Person in objecting to, contesting or opposing), such use of cash collateral or DIP Financing, (ii) shall not request or accept adequate protection or any other relief in connection therewith except as expressly permitted by Section 6.3, and (iii) shall subordinate (and hereby subordinates) its Liens in the Collateral to the Liens securing such DIP Financing (and to any “carve-out” for professional fees and United States Trustee fees agreed to by the First Lien Agent) and to any adequate protection Liens granted to the First Lien Secured Parties, on the same basis as the Second Lien Liens are subordinated to the First Lien Liens hereunder; __provided__ that, in the case of DIP Financing, (A) the aggregate principal amount of such DIP Financing (including any “roll-up” of First Lien Obligations), together with the aggregate principal amount of First Lien Obligations not so rolled up, does not exceed the sum of (1) the aggregate amount of all First Lien Obligations outstanding on the date of commencement of such Insolvency Proceeding (including principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium), Letter of Credit Obligations, Protective Advances, Hedging Obligations and Cash Management Obligations) [plus the aggregate amount of any unused Revolving Commitments on such date] plus (2) $30,000,000 (the “**DIP Cap**”), it being understood that interest, fees, premiums and expenses accruing or payable in respect of such DIP Financing or the First Lien Obligations after the commencement of such Insolvency Proceeding, and any carve-out, shall not count against the DIP Cap, and (B) such DIP Financing is secured by Liens on the Collateral that have priority equal to or senior to the First Lien Liens.
I: (b) The Second Lien Agent and the other Second Lien Secured Parties shall consent to the use of cash collateral by any Grantor in any Insolvency Proceeding if such use is consented to by the First Lien Agent, and shall not object to the use of cash collateral on the basis that their interests in the Collateral are not adequately protected.
I: (c) No Second Lien Secured Party shall, directly or indirectly, provide, offer to provide, seek, propose or support any DIP Financing (or any use of cash collateral) secured by Liens on the Collateral that are senior to or pari passu with the First Lien Liens (or that would prime the First Lien Liens or the Liens securing any DIP Financing permitted hereunder) unless the First Lien Agent has consented thereto in writing in its sole discretion, and no Second Lien Secured Party shall object to any DIP Financing permitted by Section 6.1(a) on the ground of the failure to provide “adequate protection” or otherwise.
N: DIP cap per instruction §6(a): outstanding First Lien Obligations plus $30,000,000 of new money. Conflict: Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(b) caps consented DIP financing at the “aggregate __principal amount__ outstanding under the First Lien Credit Agreement at the time of the filing” plus $30,000,000 — i.e., Trident’s principal-only position. This Agreement controls (Second Lien Credit Agreement §§6.03 and 11.02(c)), but §9.18(b) should be conformed before signing to avoid an argument that the Second Lien Lenders never authorized the broader consent. The bracketed addition of unused Revolving Commitments goes beyond the instructions: the $55,000,000 revolver is undrawn at closing, so if it is not drawn pre-petition, any revolver availability in a distress case would have to come out of the $30,000,000 new-money basket. Partner decision. Exclusion of post-petition interest, fees and the carve-out from the cap is a first-lien-favorable addition.
S: 6.2|Relief from the Automatic Stay|Until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations, the Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that none of them shall (a) seek relief from the automatic stay or any other stay in any Insolvency Proceeding in respect of the Collateral, without the prior written consent of the First Lien Agent, or (b) oppose, contest or object to any request by the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party for relief from such stay.
S: 6.3|Adequate Protection|(a) The Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that none of them shall contest, or support any other Person in contesting, (i) any request by the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties for adequate protection (in any form) or (ii) any objection by the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties to any motion, relief, action or proceeding based on the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties claiming a lack of adequate protection.
I: (b) In any Insolvency Proceeding, the Second Lien Secured Parties shall be entitled to seek and receive adequate protection solely in the form of, and shall not seek or accept adequate protection in any form other than: (i) a replacement Lien on the Collateral (and on any additional collateral on which the First Lien Agent is granted an adequate protection Lien), which Lien shall be junior and subordinate in all respects to the First Lien Liens, the Liens securing any DIP Financing (and any carve-out) and all adequate protection Liens granted to the First Lien Secured Parties, and shall be subject to this Agreement as a Second Lien Lien; and (ii) a superpriority administrative expense claim under Section 507(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, which claim shall be junior and subordinate in all respects to all superpriority claims granted to the First Lien Secured Parties (including on account of adequate protection) and to the superpriority claims of the lenders under any DIP Financing (and any carve-out); __provided__ that, in each case, the First Lien Agent is also granted (or has been granted) a senior adequate protection Lien and senior superpriority claim, as applicable.
I: (c) Without limiting Section 6.3(b), no Second Lien Secured Party shall seek or accept, and each Second Lien Secured Party hereby irrevocably waives any right to, adequate protection in the form of (i) any payment of cash (whether as current interest, fees, expenses, principal or otherwise, including any payment of fees and expenses of counsel or advisors to any Second Lien Secured Party), (ii) any Lien on or security interest in any additional collateral (other than as expressly provided in Section 6.3(b)(i)), or (iii) any administrative expense or superpriority claim that is pari passu with or senior to any claim of the First Lien Secured Parties. Any adequate protection received by any Second Lien Secured Party in contravention hereof shall be subject to Section 4.3.
N: Per instruction §6(b): replacement Liens and junior superpriority claims only; no cash payments, additional collateral or senior/equal administrative priority. Drafted without hedging, as instructed. Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(c) is consistent as to form but silent on cash payments; the express waiver in clause (c) should be expected to draw Caldwell Reed’s request for payment of their advisors’ fees. The proviso to clause (b) (second lien adequate protection only if the First Lien also receives it) is a standard first-lien-favorable condition.
S: 6.4|Avoidance Issues; Reinstatement|If any First Lien Secured Party is required in any Insolvency Proceeding or otherwise to disgorge, turn over or otherwise pay to the estate of any Grantor (or any trustee, receiver or similar Person therefor), because such amount was avoided or ordered to be paid or disgorged for any reason, including because it was found to be a fraudulent or preferential transfer, any amount (a “**Recovery**”), whether received as proceeds of security, enforcement of any right of set-off or otherwise, then the First Lien Obligations shall be reinstated to the extent of such Recovery and deemed to be outstanding as if such payment had not occurred, the Discharge of First Lien Obligations shall be deemed not to have occurred, and the First Lien Secured Parties shall be entitled to the benefits of this Agreement until a Discharge of First Lien Obligations with respect to all such recovered amounts. If this Agreement shall have been terminated prior to such Recovery, this Agreement shall be reinstated in full force and effect, and such prior termination shall not diminish, release, discharge, impair or otherwise affect the obligations of the parties hereto from such date of reinstatement. Any amounts received by any Second Lien Secured Party on account of the Second Lien Obligations after the termination of this Agreement shall, in the event of a reinstatement hereof, be held in trust for and paid over to the First Lien Agent to the extent necessary to give effect hereto.
S: 6.5|Plan Voting; Competing Plans|(a) The Second Lien Agent and the other Second Lien Secured Parties may vote on any plan of reorganization or liquidation in any Insolvency Proceeding; __provided__ that no Second Lien Secured Party shall vote in favor of, or otherwise directly or indirectly support (including by entering into any plan support or restructuring support agreement with respect to), any plan of reorganization or liquidation that is not accepted by the class or classes of holders of First Lien Obligations (or, if the First Lien Obligations are not separately classified, by the First Lien Agent at the direction of the Required First Lien Lenders), unless such plan provides for the Discharge of First Lien Obligations in cash on the effective date of such plan.
I: (b) No Second Lien Secured Party shall propose, file, sponsor or solicit acceptances of, or support any other Person (other than the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders) in proposing, any plan of reorganization or liquidation (i) at any time during the Standstill Period or (ii) at any time, that is inconsistent with the priorities or other provisions of this Agreement or that does not provide for the Discharge of First Lien Obligations in cash on the effective date thereof, unless such plan is supported by the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders.
I: (c) No Second Lien Secured Party shall object to, or support any other Person in objecting to, the confirmation of any plan of reorganization that is supported by the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders on any ground that could not be asserted by an unsecured creditor that is not party to this Agreement, and no Second Lien Secured Party shall object to any disclosure statement or other solicitation in respect of any such plan.
I: (d) To the extent that the provisions of Section 6.5(a) are not enforceable under applicable law with respect to any vote of a Second Lien Secured Party, then any distribution received by any Second Lien Secured Party under any plan in respect of Collateral or Second Lien Obligations that is inconsistent with this Agreement shall be subject to Sections 4.3 and 6.7.
N: Per instruction §6(c), drafted broadly: no vote in favor of any plan not accepted by the First Lien class unless the First Lien is paid in full in cash; no competing plan during the 180-day Standstill Period (expanded in clause (b)(ii) to plans inconsistent with this Agreement at any time, consistent with Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(e), second sentence). Conflict to expect: Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(e) states that the Second Lien Lenders “retain all rights to vote on any plan of reorganization to the extent such rights cannot be waived under applicable law.” Some bankruptcy courts have declined to enforce intercreditor provisions that strip a junior creditor’s right to vote (see, e.g., __In re 203 North LaSalle Street Partnership__, 246 B.R. 325 (Bankr. N.D. Ill. 2000)) [confirm current authority, including in the S.D.N.Y. and D. Del.], while §510(a) of the Bankruptcy Code enforces subordination agreements to the same extent as under applicable nonbankruptcy law. Clause (d) and Section 6.7 are designed so that the economic result holds even if the vote restriction is not enforced. Clause (c) (no confirmation objections other than as an unsecured creditor) is a first-lien-favorable addition.
S: 6.6|Post-Petition Interest|(a) No Second Lien Secured Party shall oppose or seek to challenge any claim by the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party for allowance in any Insolvency Proceeding of First Lien Obligations consisting of post-petition interest, fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium) or expenses, to the extent of the value of any Lien securing the First Lien Obligations, without regard to the existence of the Second Lien Liens.
I: (b) The First Lien Agent and the other First Lien Secured Parties shall not oppose or seek to challenge any claim by the Second Lien Agent for allowance in any Insolvency Proceeding of Second Lien Obligations consisting of post-petition interest, fees or expenses to the extent of the value of the Second Lien Liens on the Collateral, after taking into account the First Lien Liens and the full amount of the First Lien Obligations (including post-petition interest, fees, premiums and expenses); __provided__ that no such interest, fees or expenses shall be paid in cash prior to the Discharge of First Lien Obligations.
S: 6.7|Separate Grants of Security and Separate Classification|The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of each other Second Lien Secured Party, acknowledges and agrees that (a) the grants of Liens pursuant to the First Lien Security Documents and the Second Lien Security Documents constitute two separate and distinct grants of Liens and (b) because of, among other things, their differing rights in the Collateral, the Second Lien Obligations are fundamentally different from the First Lien Obligations and must be separately classified in any plan of reorganization proposed or adopted in an Insolvency Proceeding. S: 6.8|Section 363 Sales; Credit Bids|(a) The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that it shall not object to, oppose or otherwise contest (or support any other Person in contesting) any sale or other disposition of any Collateral free and clear of the Second Lien Liens or other claims under Section 363 of the Bankruptcy Code (or any similar provision of any other Bankruptcy Law), or any bidding or sale procedures in connection therewith, if the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders have consented to such sale, disposition or procedures, and the Second Lien Secured Parties shall be deemed to have consented under Section 363(f) of the Bankruptcy Code to any such sale, and all Second Lien Liens shall attach to the Proceeds thereof subject to Section 4.1; __provided__ that the Second Lien Agent may raise any objection to any such sale that could be raised by an unsecured creditor and that is not inconsistent with this Agreement.
I: (b) The First Lien Agent shall have the right to credit bid all or any portion of the First Lien Obligations (including under Section 363(k) of the Bankruptcy Code), and no Second Lien Secured Party shall object thereto. No Second Lien Secured Party shall credit bid any Second Lien Obligations in respect of any Collateral unless such credit bid provides for the Discharge of First Lien Obligations in cash at the closing of such sale.
S: 6.9|Section 1111(b) Waiver; No Challenge|The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of the other Second Lien Secured Parties, waives any claim it may hereafter have against any First Lien Secured Party arising out of (a) the election by any First Lien Secured Party of the application of Section 1111(b)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code, or (b) any use of cash collateral or financing arrangement, or any grant of a security interest in the Collateral, in any Insolvency Proceeding, in each case to the extent consistent with this Agreement. S: 6.10|No Waiver|Nothing contained herein shall prohibit or in any way limit the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party from objecting in any Insolvency Proceeding or otherwise to any action taken by any Second Lien Secured Party, including the seeking by any Second Lien Secured Party of adequate protection or the assertion by any Second Lien Secured Party of any of its rights and remedies under the Second Lien Documents or otherwise.
S: 6.11|Reorganization Securities|If, in any Insolvency Proceeding, debt obligations of the reorganized debtor secured by Liens upon any property of the reorganized debtor are distributed pursuant to a plan of reorganization or similar dispositive restructuring plan, both on account of First Lien Obligations and on account of Second Lien Obligations, then, to the extent the debt obligations distributed on account of the First Lien Obligations and on account of the Second Lien Obligations are secured by Liens upon the same property, the provisions of this Agreement will survive the distribution of such debt obligations pursuant to such plan and will apply with like effect to the Liens securing such debt obligations.
S: 6.12|Effectiveness in Insolvency Proceedings|This Agreement, which the parties hereto expressly acknowledge is a “subordination agreement” under Section 510(a) of the Bankruptcy Code, shall be effective before, during and after the commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding. All references in this Agreement to any Grantor shall include such Grantor as a debtor-in-possession and any receiver or trustee for such Grantor.
H1: ARTICLE VII — PURCHASE OPTION
S: 7.1|Right to Purchase|(a) Upon the occurrence of (i) the acceleration of the First Lien Obligations in accordance with the First Lien Credit Agreement (including any automatic acceleration under Section 8.02(b) thereof) or (ii) the commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding by or against the Borrower (each, a “**Purchase Event**”), the First Lien Agent shall deliver written notice of the occurrence thereof to the Second Lien Agent (a “**Purchase Event Notice**”). The Second Lien Lenders (or any of them that elect to participate, the “**Purchasing Parties**”) shall have the right, but not the obligation, exercisable by irrevocable written notice (a “**Purchase Notice**”) delivered by the Second Lien Agent on behalf of the Purchasing Parties to the First Lien Agent not later than thirty (30) Business Days after receipt of the Purchase Event Notice, to purchase from the First Lien Secured Parties all (but not less than all) of the First Lien Obligations (including all of the commitments, Hedging Obligations and Cash Management Obligations, and all participations in letters of credit) outstanding on the date of purchase. If the Second Lien Agent does not deliver a Purchase Notice within such period, the purchase right under this Article VII in respect of such Purchase Event shall terminate.
I: (b) The purchase right may be exercised only for all of the First Lien Obligations and not for any tranche, facility, class or lender position (or any portion thereof). No First Lien Secured Party shall be required to sell its First Lien Obligations other than as part of a purchase of all First Lien Obligations by the Purchasing Parties. The delivery of a Purchase Notice shall not suspend or limit the right of the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties to exercise remedies during the period prior to the closing of the purchase; __provided__ that, from the delivery of a Purchase Notice until the earlier of the closing of the purchase and the date that is ten (10) Business Days thereafter, the First Lien Agent shall not complete a foreclosure sale of all or substantially all of the Collateral (other than any disposition of perishable Collateral or Collateral threatening to decline speedily in value, or any action in an Insolvency Proceeding).
S: 7.2|Purchase Price|The purchase price shall be payable in cash in immediately available funds and shall be equal to the full amount of the First Lien Obligations, being the sum of (a) 100% of the principal amount of all loans and unreimbursed letter of credit drawings outstanding under the First Lien Documents, (b) all accrued and unpaid interest thereon (including interest at the Default Rate and post-petition interest, whether or not allowed), (c) all fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium, which for this purpose shall be deemed due and payable as if the term loans were prepaid on the date of purchase), costs, expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses) and indemnities then due and owing, (d) all amounts owing to the Hedge Counterparties in respect of Hedging Obligations (including any termination payment that would be payable if the applicable Swap Contracts were terminated on the date of purchase) and all Cash Management Obligations (or, at the election of the applicable Cash Management Bank, cash collateral therefor in an amount reasonably determined by it), (e) cash collateral for all outstanding letters of credit in an amount equal to 105% of the aggregate undrawn face amount thereof, and (f) a cash reserve, in an amount reasonably determined by the First Lien Agent, for contingent indemnification obligations of the Grantors in respect of claims asserted or reasonably expected to be asserted.
N: Conflict in our favor. Instruction §7 describes the price as “par plus accrued and unpaid interest plus any fees then due and owing.” Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(g) — Trident’s own document — sets the price at “the full amount of the First Lien Obligations, including … all fees (including any applicable premiums), and all other amounts owing in respect thereof.” The narrower instruction formulation could be read to exclude the 1.00% Prepayment Premium (applicable through October 15, 2026, including on acceleration and in any Insolvency Proceeding under First Lien Credit Agreement §2.08(e)), hedge termination amounts, cash management exposure, LC cash collateral and expenses. Because the purchase must cover “all” First Lien Obligations, including hedging and cash management, the draft follows the full-amount formulation. Recommend we do not offer the narrower version.
S: 7.3|Closing Mechanics|(a) The closing of the purchase shall occur on the date specified in the Purchase Notice, which shall be not less than five (5) and not more than ten (10) Business Days after delivery thereof. On such date, (i) the Purchasing Parties shall pay the purchase price to the First Lien Agent for distribution in accordance with the First Lien Documents, (ii) the Purchasing Parties shall assume all commitments of the First Lien Lenders (including the Revolving Commitments and letter of credit participations) and shall indemnify the First Lien Secured Parties against all losses, liabilities and expenses arising from the First Lien Obligations after the closing (including on account of any letters of credit and any checks or other payments provisionally credited and subsequently returned), and (iii) the First Lien Secured Parties shall assign the First Lien Obligations to the Purchasing Parties pursuant to the standard form of assignment and assumption under the First Lien Credit Agreement.
I: (b) Such purchase shall be expressly made without representation or warranty of any kind by the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party and without recourse of any kind, except that each First Lien Secured Party shall represent and warrant only (i) the amount of the First Lien Obligations being purchased from it, (ii) that it owns such First Lien Obligations free and clear of any Liens created by it and (iii) that it has the right to assign such First Lien Obligations and the assignment is duly authorized. Upon the closing, the First Lien Agent shall resign and the Purchasing Parties shall appoint a successor agent in accordance with the First Lien Credit Agreement, and the First Lien Agent and the resigning First Lien Secured Parties shall retain all rights to indemnification and expense reimbursement under the First Lien Documents for matters arising prior to the closing.
N: Per instruction §7: all-but-not-less-than-all, exercisable after acceleration or a bankruptcy filing, within 30 Business Days after the First Lien Agent’s notice. Note that the exercise period runs only from delivery of the First Lien Agent’s Purchase Event Notice; we have imposed an obligation on the First Lien Agent to deliver it, without a fixed deadline (Caldwell Reed will likely ask for one, e.g., five Business Days). The 10-Business Day foreclosure stand-down in Section 7.1(b) is a market concession included to preserve enforceability of the option; you may wish to delete it for the first draft.
H1: ARTICLE VIII — RELIANCE; WAIVERS; ETC.
S: 8.1|Reliance; Information|The consent by the First Lien Secured Parties to the execution and delivery of the Second Lien Documents and the grant to the Second Lien Agent of a Lien on the Collateral, and all loans and other extensions of credit made by any First Lien Secured Party, shall be deemed to have been given and made in reliance upon this Agreement. Each Secured Party has, independently and without reliance on any other Secured Party, made its own credit analysis and decision to enter into its respective credit documents and this Agreement. The First Lien Secured Parties shall have no duty to disclose to any Second Lien Secured Party any information relating to any Grantor or the Collateral.
S: 8.2|No Warranties or Liability|The Second Lien Agent acknowledges and agrees that none of the First Lien Agent or the other First Lien Secured Parties has made any express or implied representation or warranty, including with respect to the execution, validity, legality, completeness, collectability or enforceability of any of the First Lien Documents, the ownership of any Collateral or the perfection or priority of any Liens thereon. The First Lien Secured Parties will be entitled to manage and supervise their respective loans and extensions of credit under the First Lien Documents in accordance with law and as they may otherwise, in their sole discretion, deem appropriate, and shall have no duty to the Second Lien Secured Parties to act or refrain from acting in a manner that allows, or results in, the occurrence or continuance of an event of default under any agreement with any Grantor (including the Second Lien Documents). The First Lien Secured Parties shall have no liability to any Second Lien Secured Party for any action taken or omitted in accordance with this Agreement.
S: 8.3|Obligations Unconditional|All rights, interests, agreements and obligations of the First Lien Agent and the First Lien Secured Parties, and of the Second Lien Agent and the Second Lien Secured Parties, hereunder shall remain in full force and effect irrespective of (a) any lack of validity or enforceability of any First Lien Document or Second Lien Document, (b) any change in the time, manner or place of payment of, or in any other terms of, all or any of the First Lien Obligations or Second Lien Obligations, or any amendment or waiver or other modification thereof, (c) any exchange of any security interest in any Collateral or any other collateral, or any release, amendment or waiver of any guarantee, (d) the commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding in respect of any Grantor or (e) any other circumstances that otherwise might constitute a defense available to, or a discharge of, any Grantor in respect of the First Lien Obligations, or of the Second Lien Secured Parties in respect of this Agreement.
S: 8.4|Subrogation|The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of the other Second Lien Secured Parties, hereby waives any rights of subrogation it may acquire as a result of any payment hereunder until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations has occurred; __provided__ that, upon the Discharge of First Lien Obligations, the Second Lien Secured Parties shall be subrogated to the rights of the First Lien Secured Parties with respect to any payments or distributions turned over to the First Lien Agent hereunder, without recourse, representation or warranty.

H1: ARTICLE VI — INSOLVENCY PROCEEDINGS
S: 6.1|DIP Financing; Use of Cash Collateral|(a) Until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations has occurred, if any Grantor shall be subject to any Insolvency Proceeding and the First Lien Agent shall desire to permit the use of cash collateral (as such term is defined in Section 363(a) of the Bankruptcy Code) on which the First Lien Agent or any other creditor has a Lien, or to permit any Grantor to obtain financing, whether from the First Lien Secured Parties or any other Person, under Section 364 of the Bankruptcy Code or any similar provision of any other Bankruptcy Law (each, a “**DIP Financing**”), then the Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that it (i) consents to, and shall not object to, contest or otherwise oppose (or support any other Person in objecting to, contesting or opposing), such use of cash collateral or DIP Financing, (ii) shall not request or accept adequate protection or any other relief in connection therewith except as expressly permitted by Section 6.3, and (iii) shall subordinate (and hereby subordinates) its Liens in the Collateral to the Liens securing such DIP Financing (and to any “carve-out” for professional fees and United States Trustee fees agreed to by the First Lien Agent) and to any adequate protection Liens granted to the First Lien Secured Parties, on the same basis as the Second Lien Liens are subordinated to the First Lien Liens hereunder; __provided__ that, in the case of DIP Financing, (A) the aggregate principal amount of such DIP Financing (including any “roll-up” of First Lien Obligations), together with the aggregate principal amount of First Lien Obligations not so rolled up, does not exceed the sum of (1) the aggregate amount of all First Lien Obligations outstanding on the date of commencement of such Insolvency Proceeding (including principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium), Letter of Credit Obligations, Protective Advances, Hedging Obligations and Cash Management Obligations) [plus the aggregate amount of any unused Revolving Commitments on such date] plus (2) $30,000,000 (the “**DIP Cap**”), it being understood that interest, fees, premiums and expenses accruing or payable in respect of such DIP Financing or the First Lien Obligations after the commencement of such Insolvency Proceeding, and any carve-out, shall not count against the DIP Cap, and (B) such DIP Financing is secured by Liens on the Collateral that have priority equal to or senior to the First Lien Liens.
I: (b) The Second Lien Agent and the other Second Lien Secured Parties shall consent to the use of cash collateral by any Grantor in any Insolvency Proceeding if such use is consented to by the First Lien Agent, and shall not object to the use of cash collateral on the basis that their interests in the Collateral are not adequately protected.
I: (c) No Second Lien Secured Party shall, directly or indirectly, provide, offer to provide, seek, propose or support any DIP Financing (or any use of cash collateral) secured by Liens on the Collateral that are senior to or pari passu with the First Lien Liens (or that would prime the First Lien Liens or the Liens securing any DIP Financing permitted hereunder) unless the First Lien Agent has consented thereto in writing in its sole discretion, and no Second Lien Secured Party shall object to any DIP Financing permitted by Section 6.1(a) on the ground of the failure to provide “adequate protection” or otherwise.
N: DIP cap per instruction §6(a): outstanding First Lien Obligations plus $30,000,000 of new money. Conflict: Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(b) caps consented DIP financing at the “aggregate __principal amount__ outstanding under the First Lien Credit Agreement at the time of the filing” plus $30,000,000 — i.e., Trident’s principal-only position. This Agreement controls (Second Lien Credit Agreement §§6.03 and 11.02(c)), but §9.18(b) should be conformed before signing to avoid an argument that the Second Lien Lenders never authorized the broader consent. The bracketed addition of unused Revolving Commitments goes beyond the instructions: the $55,000,000 revolver is undrawn at closing, so if it is not drawn pre-petition, any revolver availability in a distress case would have to come out of the $30,000,000 new-money basket. Partner decision. Exclusion of post-petition interest, fees and the carve-out from the cap is a first-lien-favorable addition.
S: 6.2|Relief from the Automatic Stay|Until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations, the Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that none of them shall (a) seek relief from the automatic stay or any other stay in any Insolvency Proceeding in respect of the Collateral, without the prior written consent of the First Lien Agent, or (b) oppose, contest or object to any request by the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party for relief from such stay.
S: 6.3|Adequate Protection|(a) The Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that none of them shall contest, or support any other Person in contesting, (i) any request by the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties for adequate protection (in any form) or (ii) any objection by the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties to any motion, relief, action or proceeding based on the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties claiming a lack of adequate protection.
I: (b) In any Insolvency Proceeding, the Second Lien Secured Parties shall be entitled to seek and receive adequate protection solely in the form of, and shall not seek or accept adequate protection in any form other than: (i) a replacement Lien on the Collateral (and on any additional collateral on which the First Lien Agent is granted an adequate protection Lien), which Lien shall be junior and subordinate in all respects to the First Lien Liens, the Liens securing any DIP Financing (and any carve-out) and all adequate protection Liens granted to the First Lien Secured Parties, and shall be subject to this Agreement as a Second Lien Lien; and (ii) a superpriority administrative expense claim under Section 507(b) of the Bankruptcy Code, which claim shall be junior and subordinate in all respects to all superpriority claims granted to the First Lien Secured Parties (including on account of adequate protection) and to the superpriority claims of the lenders under any DIP Financing (and any carve-out); __provided__ that, in each case, the First Lien Agent is also granted (or has been granted) a senior adequate protection Lien and senior superpriority claim, as applicable.
I: (c) Without limiting Section 6.3(b), no Second Lien Secured Party shall seek or accept, and each Second Lien Secured Party hereby irrevocably waives any right to, adequate protection in the form of (i) any payment of cash (whether as current interest, fees, expenses, principal or otherwise, including any payment of fees and expenses of counsel or advisors to any Second Lien Secured Party), (ii) any Lien on or security interest in any additional collateral (other than as expressly provided in Section 6.3(b)(i)), or (iii) any administrative expense or superpriority claim that is pari passu with or senior to any claim of the First Lien Secured Parties. Any adequate protection received by any Second Lien Secured Party in contravention hereof shall be subject to Section 4.3.
N: Per instruction §6(b): replacement Liens and junior superpriority claims only; no cash payments, additional collateral or senior/equal administrative priority. Drafted without hedging, as instructed. Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(c) is consistent as to form but silent on cash payments; the express waiver in clause (c) should be expected to draw Caldwell Reed’s request for payment of their advisors’ fees. The proviso to clause (b) (second lien adequate protection only if the First Lien also receives it) is a standard first-lien-favorable condition.
S: 6.4|Avoidance Issues; Reinstatement|If any First Lien Secured Party is required in any Insolvency Proceeding or otherwise to disgorge, turn over or otherwise pay to the estate of any Grantor (or any trustee, receiver or similar Person therefor), because such amount was avoided or ordered to be paid or disgorged for any reason, including because it was found to be a fraudulent or preferential transfer, any amount (a “**Recovery**”), whether received as proceeds of security, enforcement of any right of set-off or otherwise, then the First Lien Obligations shall be reinstated to the extent of such Recovery and deemed to be outstanding as if such payment had not occurred, the Discharge of First Lien Obligations shall be deemed not to have occurred, and the First Lien Secured Parties shall be entitled to the benefits of this Agreement until a Discharge of First Lien Obligations with respect to all such recovered amounts. Any amounts received by any Second Lien Secured Party on account of the Second Lien Obligations after the termination of this Agreement shall, in the event of a reinstatement hereof, be held in trust for and paid over to the First Lien Agent to the extent necessary to give effect hereto.
S: 6.5|Plan Voting; Competing Plans|(a) The Second Lien Agent and the other Second Lien Secured Parties may vote on any plan of reorganization or liquidation in any Insolvency Proceeding; __provided__ that no Second Lien Secured Party shall vote in favor of, or otherwise directly or indirectly support (including by entering into any plan support or restructuring support agreement with respect to), any plan of reorganization or liquidation that is not accepted by the class or classes of holders of First Lien Obligations (or, if the First Lien Obligations are not separately classified, by the First Lien Agent at the direction of the Required First Lien Lenders), unless such plan provides for the Discharge of First Lien Obligations in cash on the effective date of such plan.
I: (b) No Second Lien Secured Party shall propose, file, sponsor or solicit acceptances of, or support any other Person (other than the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders) in proposing, any plan of reorganization or liquidation (i) at any time during the Standstill Period or (ii) at any time, that is inconsistent with the priorities or other provisions of this Agreement or that does not provide for the Discharge of First Lien Obligations in cash on the effective date thereof, unless such plan is supported by the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders.
I: (c) No Second Lien Secured Party shall object to, or support any other Person in objecting to, the confirmation of any plan of reorganization that is supported by the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders on any ground that could not be asserted by an unsecured creditor that is not party to this Agreement, and no Second Lien Secured Party shall object to any disclosure statement or other solicitation in respect of any such plan.
I: (d) To the extent that the provisions of Section 6.5(a) are not enforceable under applicable law with respect to any vote of a Second Lien Secured Party, then any distribution received by any Second Lien Secured Party under any plan in respect of Collateral or Second Lien Obligations that is inconsistent with this Agreement shall be subject to Sections 4.3 and 6.7.
N: Per instruction §6(c), drafted broadly: no vote in favor of any plan not accepted by the First Lien class unless the First Lien is paid in full in cash; no competing plan during the 180-day Standstill Period (expanded in clause (b)(ii) to plans inconsistent with this Agreement at any time, consistent with Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(e), second sentence). Conflict to expect: Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(e) states that the Second Lien Lenders “retain all rights to vote on any plan of reorganization to the extent such rights cannot be waived under applicable law.” Some bankruptcy courts have declined to enforce intercreditor provisions that strip a junior creditor’s right to vote (see, e.g., __In re 203 North LaSalle Street Partnership__, 246 B.R. 325 (Bankr. N.D. Ill. 2000)) [confirm current authority, including in the S.D.N.Y. and D. Del.], while §510(a) of the Bankruptcy Code enforces subordination agreements to the same extent as under applicable nonbankruptcy law. Clause (d) and Section 6.7 are designed so that the economic result holds even if the vote restriction is not enforced. Clause (c) (no confirmation objections other than as an unsecured creditor) is a first-lien-favorable addition.
S: 6.6|Post-Petition Interest|(a) No Second Lien Secured Party shall oppose or seek to challenge any claim by the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party for allowance in any Insolvency Proceeding of First Lien Obligations consisting of post-petition interest, fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium) or expenses, to the extent of the value of any Lien securing the First Lien Obligations, without regard to the existence of the Second Lien Liens.
I: (b) The First Lien Agent and the other First Lien Secured Parties shall not oppose or seek to challenge any claim by the Second Lien Agent for allowance in any Insolvency Proceeding of Second Lien Obligations consisting of post-petition interest, fees or expenses to the extent of the value of the Second Lien Liens on the Collateral, after taking into account the First Lien Liens and the full amount of the First Lien Obligations (including post-petition interest, fees, premiums and expenses); __provided__ that no such interest, fees or expenses shall be paid in cash prior to the Discharge of First Lien Obligations.
S: 6.7|Separate Grants of Security and Separate Classification|The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of each other Second Lien Secured Party, acknowledges and agrees that (a) the grants of Liens pursuant to the First Lien Security Documents and the Second Lien Security Documents constitute two separate and distinct grants of Liens and (b) because of, among other things, their differing rights in the Collateral, the Second Lien Obligations are fundamentally different from the First Lien Obligations and must be separately classified in any plan of reorganization proposed or adopted in an Insolvency Proceeding. To further effectuate the intent of the parties as provided in the immediately preceding sentence, if it is held that the claims of the First Lien Secured Parties and the Second Lien Secured Parties in respect of the Collateral constitute only one secured claim (rather than separate classes of senior and junior secured claims), then the Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of each other Second Lien Secured Party, hereby acknowledges and agrees that all distributions shall be made as if there were separate classes of senior and junior secured claims against the Grantors in respect of the Collateral, with the effect being that, to the extent that the aggregate value of the Collateral is sufficient (for this purpose ignoring all claims held by the Second Lien Secured Parties), the First Lien Secured Parties shall be entitled to receive, in addition to amounts distributed to them in respect of principal, pre-petition interest and other claims, all amounts owing in respect of post-petition interest, fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium) and expenses (whether or not allowed or allowable) before any distribution is made in respect of the Second Lien Obligations, with the Second Lien Secured Parties hereby acknowledging and agreeing to turn over to the First Lien Agent amounts otherwise received or receivable by them to the extent necessary to effectuate the intent of this sentence, even if such turnover has the effect of reducing the claim or recovery of the Second Lien Secured Parties.
S: 6.8|Section 363 Sales; Credit Bids|(a) The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that it shall not object to, oppose or otherwise contest (or support any other Person in contesting) any sale or other disposition of any Collateral free and clear of the Second Lien Liens or other claims under Section 363 of the Bankruptcy Code (or any similar provision of any other Bankruptcy Law), or any bidding or sale procedures in connection therewith, if the First Lien Agent or the Required First Lien Lenders have consented to such sale, disposition or procedures, and the Second Lien Secured Parties shall be deemed to have consented under Section 363(f) of the Bankruptcy Code to any such sale, and all Second Lien Liens shall attach to the Proceeds thereof subject to Section 4.1; __provided__ that the Second Lien Agent may raise any objection to any such sale that could be raised by an unsecured creditor and that is not inconsistent with this Agreement.
I: (b) The First Lien Agent shall have the right to credit bid all or any portion of the First Lien Obligations (including under Section 363(k) of the Bankruptcy Code), and no Second Lien Secured Party shall object thereto. No Second Lien Secured Party shall credit bid any Second Lien Obligations in respect of any Collateral unless such credit bid provides for the Discharge of First Lien Obligations in cash at the closing of such sale.
S: 6.9|Section 1111(b) Waiver; No Challenge|The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of the other Second Lien Secured Parties, waives any claim it may hereafter have against any First Lien Secured Party arising out of (a) the election by any First Lien Secured Party of the application of Section 1111(b)(2) of the Bankruptcy Code, or (b) any use of cash collateral or financing arrangement, or any grant of a security interest in the Collateral, in any Insolvency Proceeding, in each case to the extent consistent with this Agreement. No Second Lien Secured Party shall (i) assert or enforce any claim under Section 506(c) of the Bankruptcy Code senior to or on parity with the First Lien Liens for costs or expenses of preserving or disposing of any Collateral or (ii) object to, or seek to challenge, any “first day” or other orders, findings or stipulations in favor of the First Lien Secured Parties regarding the validity, perfection, priority or amount of the First Lien Obligations or the First Lien Liens.
S: 6.10|No Waiver|Nothing contained herein shall prohibit or in any way limit the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party from objecting in any Insolvency Proceeding or otherwise to any action taken by any Second Lien Secured Party, including the seeking by any Second Lien Secured Party of adequate protection or the assertion by any Second Lien Secured Party of any of its rights and remedies under the Second Lien Documents or otherwise.
S: 6.11|Reorganization Securities|If, in any Insolvency Proceeding, debt obligations of the reorganized debtor secured by Liens upon any property of the reorganized debtor are distributed pursuant to a plan of reorganization or similar dispositive restructuring plan, both on account of First Lien Obligations and on account of Second Lien Obligations, then, to the extent the debt obligations distributed on account of the First Lien Obligations and on account of the Second Lien Obligations are secured by Liens upon the same property, the provisions of this Agreement will survive the distribution of such debt obligations pursuant to such plan and will apply with like effect to the Liens securing such debt obligations.
S: 6.12|Effectiveness in Insolvency Proceedings|This Agreement, which the parties hereto expressly acknowledge is a “subordination agreement” under Section 510(a) of the Bankruptcy Code, shall be effective before, during and after the commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding. All references in this Agreement to any Grantor shall include such Grantor as a debtor-in-possession and any receiver or trustee for such Grantor.
H1: ARTICLE VII — PURCHASE OPTION
S: 7.1|Right to Purchase|(a) Upon the occurrence of (i) the acceleration of the First Lien Obligations in accordance with the First Lien Credit Agreement (including any automatic acceleration under Section 8.02(b) thereof) or (ii) the commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding by or against the Borrower (each, a “**Purchase Event**”), the First Lien Agent shall deliver written notice of the occurrence thereof to the Second Lien Agent (a “**Purchase Event Notice**”). The Second Lien Lenders (or any of them that elect to participate, the “**Purchasing Parties**”) shall have the right, but not the obligation, exercisable by irrevocable written notice (a “**Purchase Notice**”) delivered by the Second Lien Agent on behalf of the Purchasing Parties to the First Lien Agent not later than thirty (30) Business Days after receipt of the Purchase Event Notice, to purchase from the First Lien Secured Parties all (but not less than all) of the First Lien Obligations (including all of the commitments, Hedging Obligations and Cash Management Obligations, and all participations in letters of credit) outstanding on the date of purchase. If the Second Lien Agent does not deliver a Purchase Notice within such period, the purchase right under this Article VII in respect of such Purchase Event shall terminate.
I: (b) The purchase right may be exercised only for all of the First Lien Obligations and not for any tranche, facility, class or lender position (or any portion thereof). No First Lien Secured Party shall be required to sell its First Lien Obligations other than as part of a purchase of all First Lien Obligations by the Purchasing Parties. The delivery of a Purchase Notice shall not suspend or limit the right of the First Lien Agent or the First Lien Secured Parties to exercise remedies during the period prior to the closing of the purchase; __provided__ that, from the delivery of a Purchase Notice until the earlier of the closing of the purchase and the date that is ten (10) Business Days thereafter, the First Lien Agent shall not complete a foreclosure sale of all or substantially all of the Collateral (other than any disposition of perishable Collateral or Collateral threatening to decline speedily in value, or any action in an Insolvency Proceeding).
S: 7.2|Purchase Price|The purchase price shall be payable in cash in immediately available funds and shall be equal to the full amount of the First Lien Obligations, being the sum of (a) 100% of the principal amount of all loans and unreimbursed letter of credit drawings outstanding under the First Lien Documents, (b) all accrued and unpaid interest thereon (including interest at the Default Rate and post-petition interest, whether or not allowed), (c) all fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium, which for this purpose shall be deemed due and payable as if the term loans were prepaid on the date of purchase), costs, expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses) and indemnities then due and owing, (d) all amounts owing to the Hedge Counterparties in respect of Hedging Obligations (including any termination payment that would be payable if the applicable Swap Contracts were terminated on the date of purchase) and all Cash Management Obligations (or, at the election of the applicable Cash Management Bank, cash collateral therefor in an amount reasonably determined by it), (e) cash collateral for all outstanding letters of credit in an amount equal to 105% of the aggregate undrawn face amount thereof, and (f) a cash reserve, in an amount reasonably determined by the First Lien Agent, for contingent indemnification obligations of the Grantors in respect of claims asserted or reasonably expected to be asserted.
N: Conflict in our favor. Instruction §7 describes the price as “par plus accrued and unpaid interest plus any fees then due and owing.” Second Lien Credit Agreement §9.18(g) — Trident’s own document — sets the price at “the full amount of the First Lien Obligations, including … all fees (including any applicable premiums), and all other amounts owing in respect thereof.” The narrower instruction formulation could be read to exclude the 1.00% Prepayment Premium (applicable through October 15, 2026, including on acceleration and in any Insolvency Proceeding under First Lien Credit Agreement §2.08(e)), hedge termination amounts, cash management exposure, LC cash collateral and expenses. Because the purchase must cover “all” First Lien Obligations, including hedging and cash management, the draft follows the full-amount formulation. Recommend we do not offer the narrower version.
S: 7.3|Closing Mechanics|(a) The closing of the purchase shall occur on the date specified in the Purchase Notice, which shall be not less than five (5) and not more than ten (10) Business Days after delivery thereof. On such date, (i) the Purchasing Parties shall pay the purchase price to the First Lien Agent for distribution in accordance with the First Lien Documents, (ii) the Purchasing Parties shall assume all commitments of the First Lien Lenders (including the Revolving Commitments and letter of credit participations) and shall indemnify the First Lien Secured Parties against all losses, liabilities and expenses arising from the First Lien Obligations after the closing (including on account of any letters of credit and any checks or other payments provisionally credited and subsequently returned), and (iii) the First Lien Secured Parties shall assign the First Lien Obligations to the Purchasing Parties pursuant to the standard form of assignment and assumption under the First Lien Credit Agreement.
I: (b) Such purchase shall be expressly made without representation or warranty of any kind by the First Lien Agent or any First Lien Secured Party and without recourse of any kind, except that each First Lien Secured Party shall represent and warrant only (i) the amount of the First Lien Obligations being purchased from it, (ii) that it owns such First Lien Obligations free and clear of any Liens created by it and (iii) that it has the right to assign such First Lien Obligations and the assignment is duly authorized. Upon the closing, the First Lien Agent shall resign and the Purchasing Parties shall appoint a successor agent in accordance with the First Lien Credit Agreement, and the First Lien Agent and the resigning First Lien Secured Parties shall retain all rights to indemnification and expense reimbursement under the First Lien Documents for matters arising prior to the closing.
N: Per instruction §7: all-but-not-less-than-all, exercisable after acceleration or a bankruptcy filing, within 30 Business Days after the First Lien Agent’s notice. Note that the exercise period runs only from delivery of the First Lien Agent’s Purchase Event Notice; we have imposed an obligation on the First Lien Agent to deliver it, without a fixed deadline (Caldwell Reed will likely ask for one, e.g., five Business Days). The 10-Business Day foreclosure stand-down in Section 7.1(b) is a market concession included to preserve enforceability of the option; you may wish to delete it for the first draft.
H1: ARTICLE VIII — RELIANCE; WAIVERS; ETC.
S: 8.1|Reliance; Information|The consent by the First Lien Secured Parties to the execution and delivery of the Second Lien Documents and the grant to the Second Lien Agent of a Lien on the Collateral, and all loans and other extensions of credit made by any First Lien Secured Party, shall be deemed to have been given and made in reliance upon this Agreement. Each Secured Party has, independently and without reliance on any other Secured Party, made its own credit analysis and decision to enter into its respective credit documents and this Agreement. The First Lien Secured Parties shall have no duty to disclose to any Second Lien Secured Party any information relating to any Grantor or the Collateral.
S: 8.2|No Warranties or Liability|The Second Lien Agent acknowledges and agrees that none of the First Lien Agent or the other First Lien Secured Parties has made any express or implied representation or warranty, including with respect to the execution, validity, legality, completeness, collectability or enforceability of any of the First Lien Documents, the ownership of any Collateral or the perfection or priority of any Liens thereon. The First Lien Secured Parties will be entitled to manage and supervise their respective loans and extensions of credit under the First Lien Documents in accordance with law and as they may otherwise, in their sole discretion, deem appropriate, and shall have no duty to the Second Lien Secured Parties to act or refrain from acting in a manner that allows, or results in, the occurrence or continuance of an event of default under any agreement with any Grantor (including the Second Lien Documents). The First Lien Secured Parties shall have no liability to any Second Lien Secured Party for any action taken or omitted in accordance with this Agreement.
S: 8.3|Obligations Unconditional|All rights, interests, agreements and obligations of the First Lien Agent and the First Lien Secured Parties, and of the Second Lien Agent and the Second Lien Secured Parties, hereunder shall remain in full force and effect irrespective of (a) any lack of validity or enforceability of any First Lien Document or Second Lien Document, (b) any change in the time, manner or place of payment of, or in any other terms of, all or any of the First Lien Obligations or Second Lien Obligations, or any amendment or waiver or other modification thereof, (c) any exchange of any security interest in any Collateral or any other collateral, or any release, amendment or waiver of any guarantee, (d) the commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding in respect of any Grantor or (e) any other circumstances that otherwise might constitute a defense available to, or a discharge of, any Grantor in respect of the First Lien Obligations, or of the Second Lien Secured Parties in respect of this Agreement.
S: 8.4|Subrogation|The Second Lien Agent, for itself and on behalf of the other Second Lien Secured Parties, hereby waives any rights of subrogation it may acquire as a result of any payment hereunder until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations has occurred; __provided__ that, upon the Discharge of First Lien Obligations, the Second Lien Secured Parties shall be subrogated to the rights of the First Lien Secured Parties with respect to any payments or distributions turned over to the First Lien Agent hereunder, without recourse, representation or warranty.

H1: ARTICLE IX — MISCELLANEOUS
S: 9.1|Conflicts|In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Agreement and the provisions of any First Lien Document or any Second Lien Document, the provisions of this Agreement shall govern and control. The parties acknowledge that Section 8.02(c) of the First Lien Credit Agreement and Sections 6.03, 8.02(b) and 11.02(c) of the Second Lien Credit Agreement provide that the exercise of remedies and the relative rights of the parties are subject to, and governed by, this Agreement.
S: 9.2|Effectiveness; Continuing Nature; Termination|This Agreement shall become effective when executed and delivered by the parties hereto. This is a continuing agreement of Lien subordination, and the First Lien Secured Parties may continue, at any time and without notice to the Second Lien Agent or any Second Lien Secured Party, to extend credit and other financial accommodations to or for the benefit of any Grantor in reliance hereon. S: 9.3|Amendments; Waivers|No amendment, modification or waiver of any provision of this Agreement, and no consent to any departure therefrom by any party hereto, shall be effective unless it is in writing signed by the First Lien Agent and the Second Lien Agent (each acting in accordance with its applicable credit agreement), and then such waiver or consent shall be effective only in the specific instance and for the specific purpose for which given; __provided__ that (a) no such amendment shall require the consent of any Grantor unless it directly and adversely affects the rights or increases the obligations of the Grantors hereunder, and (b) any joinder contemplated by Section 5.5 shall not constitute an amendment requiring the consent of any Secured Party. No failure or delay in exercising any right hereunder shall operate as a waiver thereof.
S: 9.4|Further Assurances|Each of the Second Lien Agent and the First Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the applicable Secured Parties, and each Grantor, agrees that it will execute, or will cause to be executed, any and all further documents, agreements and instruments, and take all such further actions, as may be required under any applicable law, or which the First Lien Agent may reasonably request, to effectuate the terms of this Agreement, including the relative Lien priorities provided for herein.
S: 9.5|Agreement Solely Among Secured Parties; Acknowledgment by Grantors|This Agreement is solely an agreement among the First Lien Secured Parties and the Second Lien Secured Parties defining their relative rights. Nothing in this Agreement shall create, or be construed to create, any obligation or liability of the Borrower, Holdings or any other Grantor (other than the obligations to comply with Sections 3.5, 4.2, 4.3 (to the extent applicable to any Grantor), 5.1(b), 5.4(b), 5.5 and 9.4 and to refrain from taking actions inconsistent herewith), and none of the Borrower, Holdings or any other Grantor shall have any rights hereunder (other than rights under Section 9.3(a)). S: 9.6|Governing Law|THIS AGREEMENT AND ANY CLAIM, CONTROVERSY, DISPUTE OR CAUSE OF ACTION (WHETHER IN CONTRACT OR TORT OR OTHERWISE) BASED UPON, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT AND THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY SHALL BE GOVERNED BY, AND CONSTRUED IN ACCORDANCE WITH, THE LAW OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK, WITHOUT GIVING EFFECT TO ANY CONFLICTS OF LAW PRINCIPLES THEREOF (OTHER THAN SECTIONS 5-1401 AND 5-1402 OF THE NEW YORK GENERAL OBLIGATIONS LAW).
S: 9.7|Submission to Jurisdiction; Venue; Service of Process|Each of the parties hereto irrevocably and unconditionally submits, for itself and its property, to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of the State of New York sitting in New York County and of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and any appellate court from any thereof, in any action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and each of the parties hereto irrevocably and unconditionally agrees that all claims in respect of any such action or proceeding may be heard and determined in such New York State court or, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, in such Federal court; __provided__ that nothing herein shall limit the right of the First Lien Agent to bring proceedings in any court in which an Insolvency Proceeding is pending or in any jurisdiction in which Collateral is located to the extent necessary to enforce its rights in such Collateral. Each party irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any objection to the laying of venue of any such action or proceeding in any such court and the defense of an inconvenient forum, and consents to service of process in the manner provided for notices in Section 9.9.
S: 9.8|WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL|EACH PARTY HERETO HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY LEGAL PROCEEDING DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY (WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT OR ANY OTHER THEORY). EACH PARTY HERETO (A) CERTIFIES THAT NO REPRESENTATIVE, AGENT OR ATTORNEY OF ANY OTHER PERSON HAS REPRESENTED, EXPRESSLY OR OTHERWISE, THAT SUCH OTHER PERSON WOULD NOT, IN THE EVENT OF LITIGATION, SEEK TO ENFORCE THE FOREGOING WAIVER AND (B) ACKNOWLEDGES THAT IT AND THE OTHER PARTIES HERETO HAVE BEEN INDUCED TO ENTER INTO THIS AGREEMENT BY, AMONG OTHER THINGS, THE MUTUAL WAIVERS AND CERTIFICATIONS IN THIS SECTION.
S: 9.9|Notices|All notices and other communications provided for hereunder shall be in writing and shall be delivered by hand or overnight courier service, mailed by certified or registered mail or sent by electronic mail, addressed to each party at its address set forth in the First Lien Credit Agreement (in the case of the First Lien Agent) or the Second Lien Credit Agreement (in the case of the Second Lien Agent), and, in the case of the Borrower and Holdings, at the addresses set forth in the First Lien Credit Agreement, which as of the date hereof are as follows (or such other address as any party may designate by notice to the other parties):
I: If to the First Lien Agent: Pinnacle Credit Advisors LLC, 200 Park Avenue, 25th Floor, New York, NY 10166, Attention: Agency Services Group, Email: agencyservices@pinnaclecredit.com; with a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to Ashford, Keene & Morrow LLP, [One][Two] Liberty Plaza, 53rd Floor, New York, NY 10006, Attention: [Jonathan R. Whitfield, Esq.][Garrett Whitmore, Esq.], Email: [jwhitfield@ashfordkeene.com][gwhitmore@akm-law.com].

S: 9.10|Successors and Assigns; Additional Parties|This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and the Secured Parties and their respective successors and assigns. Each First Lien Secured Party and Second Lien Secured Party, by its acceptance of the benefits of the applicable credit documents, agrees to be bound hereby (including pursuant to Section 12.14 of the First Lien Credit Agreement and Sections 9.18(a) and 11.02 of the Second Lien Credit Agreement). Any successor or replacement First Lien Agent or Second Lien Agent shall become a party hereto by executing a joinder substantially in the form of Exhibit A, and any Person that becomes a Grantor after the date hereof shall execute an acknowledgment hereof in form reasonably satisfactory to the First Lien Agent.
S: 9.11|Third-Party Beneficiaries|This Agreement and the rights and benefits hereof shall inure to the benefit of each of the parties hereto and their respective successors and assigns, and the First Lien Secured Parties and the Second Lien Secured Parties are intended third-party beneficiaries hereof. Except as set forth in the preceding sentence, no other Person (including any Grantor, any trustee in any Insolvency Proceeding, or any creditor of any Grantor) shall have or be entitled to assert rights or benefits hereunder.
S: 9.12|Severability|If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable in any respect in any jurisdiction, such provision shall be ineffective only to the extent of such invalidity, illegality or unenforceability in such jurisdiction, without invalidating the remaining provisions hereof or affecting the validity of such provision in any other jurisdiction, and the parties shall endeavor in good-faith negotiations to replace the invalid provision with a valid provision the economic effect of which comes as close as possible to that of the invalid provision.
S: 9.13|Counterparts; Electronic Execution|This Agreement may be executed in counterparts (and by different parties hereto in different counterparts), each of which shall constitute an original, but all of which when taken together shall constitute a single contract. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page of this Agreement by facsimile, electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or any other electronic means that reproduces an image of the actual executed signature page shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart. The words “execution,” “signed,” “signature” and words of like import herein shall be deemed to include electronic signatures and electronic records, each of which shall be of the same legal effect, validity or enforceability as a manually executed signature or the use of a paper-based recordkeeping system, to the extent and as provided for in any applicable law, including the Federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, the New York State Electronic Signatures and Records Act and any other similar state laws based on the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act.
S: 9.14|Integration|This Agreement, together with the First Lien Documents and the Second Lien Documents, represents the entire agreement of the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes any and all prior agreements and understandings, oral or written, relating to the subject matter hereof.
S: 9.15|Agent Capacities|Each of the First Lien Agent and the Second Lien Agent is entering into this Agreement solely in its capacities as agent under the applicable credit agreement and not in its individual capacity, and shall be entitled to all of the rights, privileges, protections and immunities afforded to it under the First Lien Credit Agreement or the Second Lien Credit Agreement, as applicable. 461:**Section 6.1 [DIP Financing; Use of Cash Collateral.]{.underline}** (a) Until the Discharge of First Lien Obligations has occurred, if any Grantor shall be subject to any Insolvency Proceeding and the First Lien Agent shall desire to permit the use of cash collateral (as such term is defined in Section 363(a) of the Bankruptcy Code) on which the First Lien Agent or any other creditor has a Lien, or to permit any Grantor to obtain financing, whether from the First Lien Secured Parties or any other Person, under Section 364 of the Bankruptcy Code or any similar provision of any other Bankruptcy Law (each, a "**DIP Financing**"), then the Second Lien Agent, on behalf of itself and the other Second Lien Secured Parties, agrees that it (i) consents to, and shall not object to, contest or otherwise oppose (or support any other Person in objecting to, contesting or opposing), such use of cash collateral or DIP Financing, (ii) shall not request or accept adequate protection or any other relief in connection therewith except as expressly permitted by Section 6.3, and (iii) shall subordinate (and hereby subordinates) its Liens in the Collateral to the Liens securing such DIP Financing (and to any "carve-out" for professional fees and United States Trustee fees agreed to by the First Lien Agent) and to any adequate protection Liens granted to the First Lien Secured Parties, on the same basis as the Second Lien Liens are subordinated to the First Lien Liens hereunder; *provided* that, in the case of DIP Financing, (A) the aggregate principal amount of such DIP Financing (including any "roll-up" of First Lien Obligations), together with the aggregate principal amount of First Lien Obligations not so rolled up, does not exceed the sum of (1) the aggregate amount of all First Lien Obligations outstanding on the date of commencement of such Insolvency Proceeding (including principal, accrued and unpaid interest, fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium), Letter of Credit Obligations, Protective Advances, Hedging Obligations and Cash Management Obligations) \[plus the aggregate amount of any unused Revolving Commitments on such date\] plus (2) \$30,000,000 (the "**DIP Cap**"), it being understood that interest, fees, premiums and expenses accruing or payable in respect of such DIP Financing or the First Lien Obligations after the commencement of such Insolvency Proceeding, and any carve-out, shall not count against the DIP Cap, and (B) such DIP Financing is secured by Liens on the Collateral that have priority equal to or senior to the First Lien Liens.
515:**Section 7.2 [Purchase Price.]{.underline}** The purchase price shall be payable in cash in immediately available funds and shall be equal to the full amount of the First Lien Obligations, being the sum of (a) 100% of the principal amount of all loans and unreimbursed letter of credit drawings outstanding under the First Lien Documents, (b) all accrued and unpaid interest thereon (including interest at the Default Rate and post-petition interest, whether or not allowed), (c) all fees, premiums (including the Prepayment Premium, which for this purpose shall be deemed due and payable as if the term loans were prepaid on the date of purchase), costs, expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses) and indemnities then due and owing, (d) all amounts owing to the Hedge Counterparties in respect of Hedging Obligations (including any termination payment that would be payable if the applicable Swap Contracts were terminated on the date of purchase) and all Cash Management Obligations (or, at the election of the applicable Cash Management Bank, cash collateral therefor in an amount reasonably determined by it), (e) cash collateral for all outstanding letters of credit in an amount equal to 105% of the aggregate undrawn face amount thereof, and (f) a cash reserve, in an amount reasonably determined by the First Lien Agent, for contingent indemnification obligations of the Grantors in respect of claims asserted or reasonably expected to be asserted.
**"Permitted Second Lien Payments"** has the meaning assigned to such term in Section 4.2(b).

**"Pledged Collateral"** means Collateral in the possession or control of the First Lien Agent (or its agents or bailees), to the extent possession or control perfects a Lien thereon, including certificated Equity Interests, instruments, deposit accounts, securities accounts and commodity accounts.
